findings.reader: A disciplined, well-scoped news report: it states the September working paper's five-point employment and 13% earnings estimates with their reference group and 2022 baseline, defines exposure as capability rather than replacement, keeps points-vs-percent arithmetic honest and explicitly illustrative, preserves confounding, coverage and review limits to the end, and converts it all into one concrete career-office question while refusing to turn a group average into a personal verdict.
findings.facts: All nine claims — sample coverage (29%, 2016–2024), record window (Q3 2025), capability-based exposure, five-point employment decline vs the bottom six deciles with 2022 reference, ~13% full-quarter earnings decline two quarters out, unresolvable field-specific confounders, LEHD omission of self-employment and graduate school, non-representative institution sample, and the no-review/no-endorsement status — verify against the Census working paper with attribution and limits preserved; factual integrity, freshness, dated change and uncertainty handling all pass.
